title: OpenAI unveils GPT-5.6 — Sol, Terra, Luna at $5/$30 per million tokens (limited preview)
summary: OpenAI on June 25, 2026 launched a limited preview of the GPT-5.6 family: flagship Sol, balanced Terra (2x cheaper than GPT-5.5) and fast Luna, priced at $5 input / $30 output per million tokens for Sol and even less for Terra and Luna — well below Anthropic's $10/$50 Claude Fable 5; Sol adds a 'max' reasoning mode and an 'ultra' sub-agent mode, is the first OpenAI model previewed under a US-government-requested access process, ships on Cerebras at up to 750 tokens/sec in July, and was framed as particularly strong on coding, cybersecurity and biology with a tightened safety stack including '100,000 GPU hours' of red-teaming.

title: OpenAI delays GPT-5.6 broad release at Trump administration's request — first US-gov't pre-launch review
summary: OpenAI on June 25, 2026 disclosed that the Trump administration asked it to stagger GPT-5.6's rollout, making the model the first US frontier release to undergo a government-requested pre-launch access process; under the deal the White House Office of the National Cyber Director and Office of Science and Technology Policy will approve customer access on a case-by-case basis during the preview, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman told staff the company will work toward broader availability in 'a couple of weeks,' and the administration took the step after determining GPT-5.6 has 'Mythos-like' capability — citing the same security concerns that triggered a Commerce Department order forcing Anthropic to suspend Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for foreign nationals earlier this month.

title: Cursor reveals 1.5T-parameter in-house coding model training on 100,000 xAI Colossus GPUs
summary: Cursor at its Compile keynote on June 24, 2026 disclosed it is training its first fully self-built frontier model — a 1.5-trillion-parameter system pre-trained from scratch on xAI's Colossus supercomputer cluster in Memphis using more than 100,000 Nvidia GPUs (10-20x the compute of prior Cursor models) and as big as Claude Opus and GPT-5.5 according to CEO Michael Truell; the model moves Cursor away from its Kimi K2.5 base to a blank initialization, is expected to ship 'within weeks,' and was unveiled alongside a Git-rival hosting platform called Origin (general availability fall 2026) and an iOS mobile app for remotely monitoring coding agents — the same day SpaceX confirmed its $60B all-stock acquisition of Cursor's parent Anysphere.

title: Google DeepMind ships Gemini Robotics On-Device — first VLA runnable on a robot without the cloud
summary: Google DeepMind on June 24, 2026 released Gemini Robotics On-Device, the first VLA (vision-language-action) model it has made available for fine-tuning and that runs locally on a robot — no cloud, no internet — with performance the team says is 'quite close' to the hybrid cloud-based Gemini Robotics released in March; the model was trained on ALOHA robots but adapted to bi-arm Franka FR3 industrial arms and Apptronik's Apollo humanoid, can be fine-tuned with as few as 50-100 demonstrations, ships with the first Gemini Robotics SDK plus MuJoCo simulator support, and is rolling out now through DeepMind's trusted-tester program with strict safety guidance for developers building always-on physical-AI applications.

title: Microsoft ships seven in-house MAI models — Thinking-1, Code-1-Flash, Image-2.5, Voice-2, Transcribe-1.5
summary: Microsoft on June 24, 2026 launched a seven-model suite developed internally by Microsoft AI (MAI) — MAI-Thinking-1 (medium-weight reasoning trained on clean data instead of third-party outputs), MAI-Code-1-Flash (agentic coding in GitHub Copilot and VS Code), MAI-Image-2.5 (ranking above Google's Nano Banana Pro), MAI-Transcribe-1.5 ('best transcription model in the world,' 5x faster than rivals), MAI-Voice-2 (15+ languages with misuse safeguards, Flash variant coming) — with a 'Frontier Tuning' system that lets enterprises customize models on proprietary data inside their compliance boundaries via a three-step reinforcement learning loop; the launch marks a strategic shift away from dependence on OpenAI and positions Microsoft to compete directly with Google and other AI labs across the full stack.

title: Cohere Command A+ debuts in Microsoft Foundry — 218B MoE reasoning model with 48-language support
summary: Cohere's open-source Command A+ (218B-parameter mixture-of-experts with 25B active) launched in Microsoft Foundry on June 24, 2026 as a serverless API offering that combines reasoning, RAG, coding and tool use in a single enterprise model; it reasons across 48 languages, processes documents with embedded images and tables, and orchestrates multi-step workflows without requiring customers to stitch multiple models together — letting Foundry developers deploy Cohere's newest model in the same environment where they build, evaluate and operate AI applications, with Microsoft's enterprise customers targeted as the primary audience given the platform's existing compliance, governance and integration tooling.

title: NVIDIA DFlash speculative decoding — 15x throughput on Blackwell at matched interactivity
summary: NVIDIA on June 24, 2026 detailed DFlash, a speculative decoding technique that drafts entire token blocks in parallel rather than one token at a time, reporting up to 15x throughput at the same user interactivity target on gpt-oss-120b across 8 Blackwell GPUs in a DGX B300 (about 1.5x more than EAGLE-3 at 500-600 tokens/sec per user); a separate NVIDIA Speed-Bench showed DFlash averaging 2.3x vs EAGLE-3's 1.7x on gpt-oss-120b and 2.8x vs EAGLE-3's 2.2x on Llama 3.1 8B Instruct — paper reports up to 6.08x lossless speedup on Qwen3-8B, with the lightweight five-layer drafter shipped on GitHub and Hugging Face (arXiv 2602.06036).

title: Microsoft ships AI wave for Education — Teach Unit Plans, Study and Learn Agent, Copilot Notebooks
summary: Microsoft on June 24, 2026 rolled out a new wave of AI-powered teaching and learning experiences inside Microsoft 365 Education ahead of ISTELive 26 — including standards-aligned Unit Plans in Teach (50+ countries), a Study and Learn Agent in Copilot Chat built on learning-science principles (scaffolded questions, interactive practice, real-time feedback) for students age 13+, and Copilot Notebooks that turn lecture slides, handouts, readings and notes into AI-powered interactive study guides; all three ship at no additional cost with Microsoft 365 Education and were announced alongside Microsoft's third annual AI in Education Report highlighting accelerating K-12 adoption.

title: OpenAI unveils 'Jalapeño' — its first custom Broadcom-built LLM inference chip
summary: OpenAI and Broadcom on June 24, 2026 unveiled Jalapeño, OpenAI's first in-house 'Intelligence Processor' for LLM inference — an ASIC co-developed with Broadcom silicon and networking (Tomahawk) and Celestica boards/racks, designed from scratch around LLM fundamentals and shipped from initial design to manufacturing tape-out in nine months (what OpenAI calls the fastest ASIC development cycle ever achieved in high-performance advanced semiconductors) with OpenAI's own models helping design parts of the chip; engineering samples are already running GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark at production target frequency and power, OpenAI reports 'substantially better' performance per watt than current state-of-the-art, and the first Jalapeño servers are targeted for end of 2026 inside gigawatt-scale deployments alongside Microsoft and other partners.

title: Mistral ships workspace-level Connector controls — multi-account GA, debugger preview, 60+ integrations
summary: Mistral on June 24, 2026 added four new enterprise connector capabilities to Studio: workspace- and org-level access controls plus per-tool toggles (GA), API keys with connector scopes to prevent impersonation (GA), multi-account connectors so a single connector can hold several authenticated identities per task (GA), a Connectors Debugger for end-to-end MCP root-cause analysis (public preview), Connectors in Vibe Code (GA) and Connectors in Workflows (public preview) — bringing the live directory to 60+ integrations, with custom MCP connectors as fallback for everything else.

title: NVIDIA ships BioNeMo Agent Toolkit — 50+ life-sciences orgs (Lilly, Anthropic, OpenAI) sign on
summary: NVIDIA on June 23, 2026 announced BioNeMo Agent Toolkit, an open set of agentic life-sciences tools/skills built on NVIDIA NIM, Parabricks, NeMo and Nemotron that lets AI agents gather evidence, reason across findings, run computational experiments and recommend next steps; Anthropic and OpenAI are integrating it, while Lilly, Schrödinger, Dassault Systèmes, Databricks, Snowflake, the UW Medicine Institute for Protein Design and dozens more are already using it — described by Jensen Huang as 'a PhD research assistant and the speed of a supercomputer,' available now via NVIDIA developer resources and GitHub.

title: Alibaba's Qwen-AgentWorld — first 7-domain language world model beats GPT-5.4 / Claude Opus 4.8 on simulation
summary: Alibaba's Qwen team released Qwen-AgentWorld on June 24, 2026, a native language world model that predicts what tools/environments return (not how to act) across seven agent domains — MCP, Search, Terminal, SWE, Web, OS and Android — in a single 35B-A3B / 397B-A17B MoE with 256K context; the 397B variant tops AgentWorldBench simulation quality versus GPT-5.4, Claude Opus 4.8 and Gemini 3.1 Pro, the 35B weights are open-sourced under Apache-2.0 on Hugging Face and ModelScope, and a paired AgentWorldBench evaluates all seven domains, with warm-up world-model training lifting BFCL v4 from 62.29 to 71.25 and Claw-Eval from 53.60 to 64.88 with no agent-specific fine-tuning.

title: Google bakes Computer Use into Gemini 3.5 Flash — replaces standalone model with built-in tool + enterprise guards
summary: Google moved Computer Use from a standalone Gemini 2.5 model into Gemini 3.5 Flash as a native tool on June 24, 2026 — letting developers build agents that see screens, click, type and scroll across browsers, mobile and desktop via the Gemini API and the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (the renamed Vertex AI), with simplified actions using intents, configurable safety policies and built-in indirect prompt-injection detection; Google also layers two opt-in enterprise safeguards on top — explicit human confirmation for sensitive actions and automatic halting when prompt injection is detected — and ships a live demo environment with Browserbase plus a reference implementation on GitHub.

title: Meta launches $299 self-branded AI smart glasses — first to ship Muse Spark, 20-language live translation
summary: Meta on June 24, 2026 unveiled its first self-branded AI smart glasses line starting at $299 ($80 cheaper than Ray-Ban Meta Gen 2), in three models — Adventurer, Fury and a Kylie Jenner collab (Meta Glasses by Kylie) with a Starfire edition at $399 — across 26 frame/lens combos; the glasses are the first devices to ship with Muse Spark, Meta Superintelligence Labs' proprietary wearable AI model, and add Dynamic Photo multi-shot AI curation plus live translation across 20 languages including Hindi, Arabic, Mandarin, Japanese and Korean — available today at Meta Lab stores, Best Buy and Meta's site.

title: Meta builds AI-driven prediction market app 'Arena' — Llama generates questions, resolves markets
summary: Meta is developing a standalone prediction-market app codenamed Arena (also called FBForecast) to compete with Kalshi and Polymarket, with internal documents reviewed by NPR and The New York Times on June 24, 2026 showing users will receive a daily 'play money' allotment to bet on yes/no real-world events, Llama will auto-generate questions from trending topics and deliver personalized market recommendations, and the same AI will resolve markets 'in near real time' (no human review, no dispute window) — the app is positioned as a 'rebuild' of Meta's 2020 Forecast app, which was wound down in 2022 due to 'the operational cost of manual question curation,' and prototypes will be tested internally before public launch on iOS and Android.

title: ByteDance rolls out paid Doubao Pro from 68 RMB — first major Chinese AI chatbot to charge, with Office Agent mode
summary: ByteDance launched paid Doubao Professional subscriptions on June 24, 2026 — the first major Chinese AI chatbot to monetize (Doubao has 300M+ MAUs) — with tiers at 68 RMB (Standard), 200 RMB (Enhanced) and 500 RMB (Premium) per month, plus a discounted 38 RMB student plan and accessible pricing for visually impaired users; the Pro edition runs the new Doubao 2.1 model, unlocks an 'Office Agent mode' that, with user authorization, can directly operate the local computer and browser for document / spreadsheet / PowerPoint work and auto-publish scheduled Weibo posts, supports cross-app automation and scheduled daily-report tasks, with backend-database building for online apps in gray-scale testing.

title: ByteDance launches Seed 2.1 Pro / Turbo at Volcano Engine FORCE — Doubao 2.1 Pro leads OSWorld, MMMU-Pro
summary: ByteDance on June 23, 2026 launched the Seed 2.1 family at the 2026 Volcano Engine FORCE conference — Doubao 2.1 Pro and a half-price Doubao 2.1 Turbo tuned for high-frequency enterprise scenarios — claiming frontier scores on Terminal Bench 2.1, SWE-Pro and SciCode and leading positions on OSWorld, MobileWorld and MMMU-Pro; Doubao 2.1 Pro is priced at 6 yuan / 1M input tokens and 30 yuan / 1M output tokens (cache-hit 1.2 yuan) with Volcano Engine claiming total cost of ownership roughly 80% lower than Claude Opus 4.6, while the Seed Full-Duplex Speech LLM is now live on Doubao App with a 12% conversational-fluency gain.

title: Perplexity launches 'Computer for Counsel' — Docusign, NetDocuments, Clio Vincent, Carta onboard via MCP
summary: Perplexity on June 24, 2026 launched Computer for Counsel, a vertical legal agentic product built on its LLM-agnostic Perplexity Computer platform and available to Enterprise and Max users, supporting NDA intake/review, regulatory dashboards and legal research; MCP integrations cover Docusign IAM for end-to-end contract automation, NetDocuments document management, Carta for cap-table data, Box, Clio's Vincent legal research (with citator analysis and authority-backed reasoning over Clio's 1B+ document corpus) plus Microsoft 365 (drafting in Word, SharePoint files, Outlook/Teams context), with LegalZoom contract templates, Deel compliance data and Midpage research wired in for limited-access workflows.

title: DeepSeek publishes DualPath — reroutes prefill traffic through idle decode NICs, doubles cluster utilization
summary: DeepSeek on June 24, 2026 released DualPath (arXiv 2602.21548), an open datacenter serving technique that loads KV-cache through idle decode-side storage NICs and hands them to prefill engines via high-bandwidth RDMA — eliminating the prefill-side storage bottleneck that caps long-context agent serving at ~40% utilization; DeepSeek's internal measurements show up to 1.87x offline throughput improvement and 1.96x average online throughput improvement (without SLO violations) versus the company's own disaggregated-prefill baseline, with a traffic-control layer that prioritizes thinking traffic over memory traffic to avoid creating a new bottleneck — landing as a big win for multi-turn agentic workloads where prefill scheduling is the choke point.

title: NVIDIA Computex keynote: Vera CPU, Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B, OpenShell sandbox, RTX Spark superchip
summary: NVIDIA at GTC Taipei during Computex 2026 (covered June 24, 2026) laid out a six-part agentic AI stack: Vera CPU 'purpose-built for agentic and RL workloads' (~2x efficiency, 50% faster than x86, with OpenAI/Anthropic/SpaceX early adopters), Vera Rubin platform ramping to full production, Nemotron 3 Ultra — a 550B-parameter open model from the Nemotron Coalition aimed at long-running agents — plus an edge/edge-tier multimodal sibling, OpenShell policy-driven agent sandbox for permissions / human sign-off / high-risk action blocking, RTX Spark laptop superchip pairing Arm + Blackwell + up to 128GB unified memory (autumn 2026), and a deskside DGX for Windows for always-on developer agents — with Huang framing agents as 'the computing pattern of the next decade.'

title: Anthropic ships Claude Tag — @Claude joins Slack as a persistent, ambient AI teammate on Opus 4.8
summary: Anthropic on June 23, 2026 launched Claude Tag, a Slack-native AI teammate that grants Claude persistent identity and memory across channels — anyone can @Claude to delegate tasks, Claude builds long-running context across the channels it has access to and can schedule work for future execution; the tool ships with an ambient mode where Claude proactively follows up on stalled threads and surfaces relevant info without being asked, and Anthropic says 65% of its own product team's code now ships through an internal Claude Tag — Claude Tag runs on Opus 4.8, replaces the existing 'Claude in Slack' app with a 30-day migration window, and is in beta today for Claude Enterprise and Team customers.

title: Mistral OCR 4 ships with bounding boxes, block labels and 170-language self-hosting
summary: Mistral released OCR 4 on June 23, 2026 as the successor to its document-intelligence model, returning bounding boxes, typed block labels (paragraph, title, list, table, image, equation, caption, code, header, footer, signature) and per-word confidence scores alongside extracted text; the model covers 170 languages across 10 groups, runs in a single container for self-hosted deployments with strict data-sovereignty requirements, ships as the ingestion layer for the open-source Mistral Search Toolkit (RAG / enterprise search) announced at AI Now Summit, is priced at $4 per 1,000 pages through the API ($2 with the Batch discount) with a $5/1k-pages Document AI option in Mistral Studio, and an internal blind review of 600+ documents picked OCR 4's output 72% of the time over competing models.

title: Microsoft ships Azure Copilot Observability Agent GA — correlates signals across agents, apps, infrastructure
summary: Microsoft announced general availability of the Azure Copilot Observability Agent on June 23, 2026, built on Azure Monitor to correlate logs, metrics, traces, topology and operational context across agentic systems, applications, infrastructure and services; the GA is positioned as a foundational layer for 'defending and operating confidently' in agentic environments where autonomous systems run for hours, with the agent reducing time-to-root-cause by joining operational signals end-to-end and streaming context to operators as conditions evolve.
